library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: Yamamoto Y, Valitalo PA, van den Berg DJ, *et al.* A Generic
  Multi-Compartmental CNS Distribution Model Structure for 9 Drugs Allows
  Prediction of Human Brain Target Site Concentrations. *Pharm Res*
  2017;34(2):333-351.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-016-2065-3> (open access,
  CC BY 4.0; PubMed Central PMC5236087)

The paper fits one common brain-distribution structure, separately, to rich
rat plasma and microdialysis data for nine drugs, and then translates the
acetaminophen and morphine fits to humans. Each of those eleven fits is a
separate model in nlmixr2lib:

```{r models}
rat_models <- c(
  acetaminophen = "Yamamoto_2017b_acetaminophen_rat",
  atenolol      = "Yamamoto_2017b_atenolol_rat",
  methotrexate  = "Yamamoto_2017b_methotrexate_rat",
  morphine      = "Yamamoto_2017b_morphine_rat",
  paliperidone  = "Yamamoto_2017b_paliperidone_rat",
  phenytoin     = "Yamamoto_2017b_phenytoin_rat",
  quinidine     = "Yamamoto_2017b_quinidine_rat",
  remoxipride   = "Yamamoto_2017b_remoxipride_rat",
  risperidone   = "Yamamoto_2017b_risperidone_rat"
)
human_models <- c(
  acetaminophen = "Yamamoto_2017b_acetaminophen_human",
  morphine      = "Yamamoto_2017b_morphine_human"
)
rat_ui <- lapply(rat_models, function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n)))
human_ui <- lapply(human_models, function(n) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(n)))
```

The same authors published a different, fully physiologically based CNS
model for the same rat data later in 2017 (Yamamoto *et al.*, *CPT
Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol* 6:765-777); it is packaged separately as the
`Yamamoto_2017_<drug>_rat_pbpk` models.

## Model structure

All eleven models share the structure of the paper's Figure 2:

* an empirical plasma model -- one compartment (paliperidone, risperidone),
  two compartments (acetaminophen, atenolol, phenytoin, quinidine,
  remoxipride, and both human models) or three compartments (methotrexate,
  morphine) -- with linear clearance;
* a brain extracellular-fluid compartment (`brain_ecf`) that receives drug
  from plasma through a one-way clearance `clin` (the paper's Q_PL_ECF);
* four cerebrospinal-fluid compartments in series -- lateral ventricle
  (`brain_csf_lv`), third + fourth ventricle (`brain_csf_tfv`), cisterna
  magna (`brain_csf_cm`) and subarachnoid space (`brain_csf_sas`). One drug
  dispersion flow `q_diff` (Q_DIFF) carries drug from brain ECF through the
  four CSF compartments and back to plasma;
* drug-specific additions where the data supported them: a brain
  intracellular-fluid compartment exchanging with brain ECF (paliperidone,
  quinidine), a one-way efflux from lateral-ventricle CSF to plasma across the
  blood-CSF barrier (methotrexate), enterohepatic recirculation
  (acetaminophen), a categorical dose effect on Q_PL_ECF (morphine), and
  transporter-inhibitor effects on Q_PL_ECF (and, for methotrexate, on the
  CSF efflux) of the form `P = P_PAT * (1 + theta * Cov)` (Eq. 3);
* brain volumes fixed to rat (Table III) or human (Table IV) physiology.

Every concentration is unbound: plasma data were converted with the measured
unbound fraction, and microdialysate was corrected for in-vivo probe
recovery. The rat fits used naive pooling, so the rat models carry no
between-animal variability. In the human models the brain-side drug
parameters are the rat estimates scaled allometrically to 70 kg (Eq. 9), so
their brain concentrations are predictions; only the plasma parameters were
estimated from human data.

# Population

**Rat (model development, Table I).** Male Wistar rats, 225-275 g, Leiden
University. Data for six drugs were previously published (acetaminophen,
atenolol, methotrexate, morphine from two studies, quinidine, remoxipride);
data for paliperidone, phenytoin and risperidone were newly produced. Each
drug was given as a short intravenous infusion and sampled in plasma and by
microdialysis in brain ECF, and for some drugs in lateral-ventricle and/or
cisterna-magna CSF, for up to 300-480 min. Six drugs were also studied with a
transporter inhibitor: probenecid (MRPs, OATs, OATPs) for methotrexate and
phenytoin, and the P-gp inhibitors GF120918 (elacridar) for morphine and
tariquidar for paliperidone, phenytoin, quinidine and risperidone.

**Human (translation, Table II and Tables SIII-SIV).** Acetaminophen:
Study 1, 7 neurointensive-care patients with an external ventricular drain
(EVD) given 1 g over 30 min, with plasma and EVD-collected CSF; Study 2, a
published mean profile of plasma and subarachnoid CSF in patients with
nerve-root compression pain after 2 g propacetamol. Morphine: two published
studies (3 patients) with traumatic brain injury given 10 mg over 10 min,
with plasma and brain-ECF microdialysis from the "normal" and the "injured"
side of the brain.

```{r population}
pop <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(rat_ui, human_ui), function(u) {
  data.frame(
    species = u$population$species,
    n_subjects = u$population$n_subjects,
    dose_range = u$population$dose_range
  )
}))
pop$model <- c(rat_models, human_models)
knitr::kable(pop[, c("model", "species", "n_subjects", "dose_range")], row.names = FALSE)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
below collects the rat estimates (Table III) as packaged.

```{r source-trace-rat}
theta_of <- function(ui, nm) {
  v <- ui$iniDf$est[match(nm, ui$iniDf$name)]
  if (is.na(v)) NA_real_ else v
}
rat_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(rat_ui), function(d) {
  u <- rat_ui[[d]]
  data.frame(
    drug = d,
    CL_PL = exp(theta_of(u, "lcl")),
    V_PL = exp(theta_of(u, "lvc")),
    Q_PL_PER1 = exp(theta_of(u, "lq")),
    V_PER1 = exp(theta_of(u, "lvp")),
    Q_PL_PER2 = exp(theta_of(u, "lq2")),
    V_PER2 = exp(theta_of(u, "lvp2")),
    Q_PL_ECF = exp(theta_of(u, "lclin")),
    Q_DIFF = exp(theta_of(u, "lq_diff")),
    Q_ECF_ICF = exp(theta_of(u, "lq_brain_ecf_brain_icf")),
    Q_LV_PL = exp(theta_of(u, "lcl_csf"))
  )
}))
knitr::kable(rat_tab, digits = 5, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Rat structural estimates as packaged (Table III; mL/min and mL). NA = not part of that drug's model.")
```

| Quantity | Source location |
|----------|-----------------|
| Model structure (compartments, flow directions) | Figure 2; Table III footnotes ("clearance from the central compartment to brainECF", "clearance from CSFLV to the central compartment", "inter-compartmental clearance between brainECF and brainICF") |
| Rat plasma, brain and residual-error estimates | Table III, one column per drug |
| Morphine Q_PL_ECF at 4 mg/kg (0.00750 mL/min) vs 10/40 mg/kg (0.00458 mL/min) | Table III footnotes c and d; Results (categorical dose effect) |
| Transporter-inhibitor effects | Table III "Impact of active transport on" rows; Eq. 3 |
| Acetaminophen enterohepatic fraction (93.3 %) | Table III "fraction" |
| Rat brain volumes (V_ECF 0.29, V_ICF 1.44, V_LV 0.05, V_TFV 0.05, V_CM 0.017, V_SAS 0.18 mL) | Table III, footnote e |
| Human plasma estimates, between-subject SDs, residual SD | Table IV |
| Human Q_PL_ECF and Q_DIFF | Table IV (allometric scaling, Eq. 9 with 70 kg and 0.25 kg) |
| Human brain volumes (V_ECF 240, V_LV 22.5, V_TFV 22.5, V_CM 7.5, V_SAS 90 mL) | Table IV, footnote a |
| EVD drainage flow Q_LV_EVD | Methods "Adding Clinical Sampling Procedure Related Fixed Parameters"; Table SIV |
| Between-subject variability model (exponential) | Eq. 6 |
| Residual error model (proportional) | Eq. 7 |

The human translation can be checked directly: Table IV's drug-specific
brain parameters should equal the rat estimates times
(70 / 0.25)^0.75 = `r signif((70 / 0.25)^0.75, 4)`.

```{r allometric-check}
scale_f <- (70 / 0.25)^0.75
allo <- data.frame(
  parameter = c("acetaminophen Q_PL_ECF", "acetaminophen Q_DIFF",
                "morphine Q_PL_ECF (4 mg/kg rat value)", "morphine Q_DIFF"),
  rat = c(exp(theta_of(rat_ui$acetaminophen, "lclin")),
          exp(theta_of(rat_ui$acetaminophen, "lq_diff")),
          exp(theta_of(rat_ui$morphine, "lclin") + theta_of(rat_ui$morphine, "e_dose_low_clin")),
          exp(theta_of(rat_ui$morphine, "lq_diff"))),
  human_table_iv = c(exp(theta_of(human_ui$acetaminophen, "lclin")),
                     exp(theta_of(human_ui$acetaminophen, "lq_diff")),
                     exp(theta_of(human_ui$morphine, "lclin")),
                     exp(theta_of(human_ui$morphine, "lq_diff")))
)
allo$rat_scaled <- allo$rat * scale_f
allo$ratio <- allo$human_table_iv / allo$rat_scaled
knitr::kable(allo, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
# Table IV prints three significant figures, so the ratio must be 1 within
# rounding. A wrong rat value or a wrong exponent moves it by far more.
stopifnot(all(abs(allo$ratio - 1) < 0.01))
```

The morphine human Q_PL_ECF (0.513 mL/min) matches the scaled **4 mg/kg**
rat value; the 10/40 mg/kg value would scale to
`r signif(0.00458 * scale_f, 3)` mL/min.

# Virtual cohort and simulation helpers

The rat models describe a typical (naive-pooled) animal, so the rat
simulations are single typical-value profiles at the body weight the paper
uses for scaling, 0.25 kg (Eq. 9). All doses are converted to ng per animal.

```{r helpers}
cov_defaults <- list(DOSE_LOW = 0L, CONMED_PROBENECID = 0L, CONMED_ELACRIDAR = 0L,
                     CONMED_TARIQUIDAR = 0L, CSF_DRAIN_VOL_24H = 0)

# One subject's event table: a zero-order infusion into `central` plus
# observation rows on the `central` state; every algebraic output (Cc,
# Cbrain_ecf, ...) is returned at those rows.
make_events <- function(id, dose_ng, dur, obs_times, covs = list()) {
  covs <- utils::modifyList(cov_defaults, covs)
  d <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(id = id, time = 0, amt = dose_ng, rate = dose_ng / dur,
                   evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tibble::tibble(id = id, time = obs_times, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_,
                   evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  )
  for (n in names(covs)) d[[n]] <- covs[[n]]
  d
}

out_cols <- c("time", "Cc", "Cbrain_ecf", "Cbrain_icf", "Cbrain_csf_lv",
              "Cbrain_csf_tfv", "Cbrain_csf_cm", "Cbrain_csf_sas")

# Typical-value solve. The rat models have no random effects; the human
# models do, and without zeroRe() a one-subject solve would draw a random
# patient rather than the typical one.
solve_typical <- function(model_name, events) {
  m <- readModelDb(model_name)
  if (any(!is.na(rxode2::rxode(m)$iniDf$neta1))) m <- rxode2::zeroRe(m)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(m, events,
                                     useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"))
  if (is.null(s$id)) s$id <- events$id[1]
  s[, intersect(c("id", out_cols), names(s))]
}

rat_design <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,           ~dose_mgkg, ~dur, ~inhibitor,
  "acetaminophen", 16,         10,   NA,
  "atenolol",      10,         1,    NA,
  "methotrexate",  40,         10,   "CONMED_PROBENECID",
  "morphine",      10,         10,   "CONMED_ELACRIDAR",
  "paliperidone",  0.5,        20,   "CONMED_TARIQUIDAR",
  "phenytoin",     30,         10,   "CONMED_TARIQUIDAR",
  "quinidine",     10,         10,   "CONMED_TARIQUIDAR",
  "remoxipride",   8,          30,   NA,
  "risperidone",   2,          20,   "CONMED_TARIQUIDAR"
)
rat_bw_kg <- 0.25
obs_rat <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 30, by = 1), seq(32, 480, by = 4))))
```

# Rat: replicate Figure 4a

Figure 4a of the paper shows the observed acetaminophen (16 mg/kg) and
morphine profiles with the mean model prediction. The acetaminophen profile
carries the enterohepatic return as a plateau after 120 min.

```{r fig4a}
sim_apap <- solve_typical(rat_models[["acetaminophen"]],
                          make_events(1L, 16 * rat_bw_kg * 1e6, 10, obs_rat))
sim_mor <- solve_typical(rat_models[["morphine"]],
                         make_events(1L, 10 * rat_bw_kg * 1e6, 10, obs_rat))
fig4a <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_apap |> dplyr::mutate(drug = "Acetaminophen 16 mg/kg") |>
    dplyr::select(drug, time, Plasma = Cc, BrainECF = Cbrain_ecf,
                  CSF_LV = Cbrain_csf_lv, CSF_CM = Cbrain_csf_cm),
  sim_mor |> dplyr::mutate(drug = "Morphine 10 mg/kg") |>
    dplyr::select(drug, time, Plasma = Cc, BrainECF = Cbrain_ecf)
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, BrainECF, CSF_LV, CSF_CM),
                      names_to = "site", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc), time > 0, time <= 250) |>
  dplyr::mutate(site = factor(site, c("Plasma", "BrainECF", "CSF_LV", "CSF_CM")))
ggplot(fig4a, aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  facet_grid(drug ~ site) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Unbound concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates the mean predictions of Figure 4a of Yamamoto 2017b (typical rat, 0.25 kg).")
```

```{r fig4a-check}
at <- function(s, tt, col) s[[col]][match(tt, s$time)]
# Read off Figure 4a: acetaminophen plasma peaks near 1e4 ng/mL and then
# plateaus near 100 ng/mL from 120 to 240 min; morphine plasma peaks near
# 5e3 ng/mL and brain ECF falls to about 20 ng/mL by 240 min. Typical-value
# solves are deterministic, so these bounds test the transcription (a wrong
# volume or a dropped recirculation would move a value by far more than 2-fold).
stopifnot(
  max(sim_apap$Cc) > 5000, max(sim_apap$Cc) < 20000,
  at(sim_apap, 240, "Cc") > 30, at(sim_apap, 240, "Cc") < 300,
  at(sim_apap, 240, "Cc") / at(sim_apap, 116, "Cc") > 0.5,
  max(sim_mor$Cc) > 2000, max(sim_mor$Cc) < 10000,
  at(sim_mor, 240, "Cbrain_ecf") > 5, at(sim_mor, 240, "Cbrain_ecf") < 60
)
```

# Rat: all nine drugs, with and without transporter inhibition

Representative dose of each study (Table I), typical animal, with and
without the inhibitor where one was studied (paper Figure S1).

```{r rat-all}
rat_runs <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(rat_design))) {
  r <- rat_design[i, ]
  arms <- if (is.na(r$inhibitor)) "none" else c("none", r$inhibitor)
  for (a in arms) {
    covs <- if (a == "none") list() else stats::setNames(list(1L), a)
    s <- solve_typical(rat_models[[r$drug]],
                       make_events(1L, r$dose_mgkg * rat_bw_kg * 1e6, r$dur, obs_rat, covs))
    s$drug <- r$drug
    s$arm <- if (a == "none") "no inhibitor" else "with inhibitor"
    rat_runs[[length(rat_runs) + 1]] <- s
  }
}
rat_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(rat_runs)
rat_all |>
  dplyr::select(drug, arm, time, Plasma = Cc, BrainECF = Cbrain_ecf) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, BrainECF), names_to = "site", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = site, linetype = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Unbound concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Typical rat profiles for the nine drugs (cf. Figure S1 of Yamamoto 2017b).")
```

## Steady-state check of the brain structure

Because drug enters brain ECF only through `clin` and leaves only through
`q_diff`, the unbound brain-ECF-to-plasma ratio at steady state is exactly
`clin / q_diff`, and the CSF compartments in series all share the ECF
concentration -- except for methotrexate, whose lateral-ventricle efflux
lowers every CSF compartment by `q_diff / (q_diff + cl_csf)`. A long constant
infusion checks the ODEs against these closed forms.

```{r steady-state}
ss_rows <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(rat_design))) {
  r <- rat_design[i, ]
  arms <- if (is.na(r$inhibitor)) "none" else c("none", r$inhibitor)
  u <- rat_ui[[r$drug]]
  for (a in arms) {
    covs <- if (a == "none") list() else stats::setNames(list(1L), a)
    ev <- make_events(1L, 1e5 * 6000, 6000, c(5990, 6000), covs)
    s <- solve_typical(rat_models[[r$drug]], ev)
    s <- s[s$time == 5990, ]
    clin <- exp(theta_of(u, "lclin"))
    eff <- if (a == "none") 0 else theta_of(u, paste0("e_", tolower(a), "_clin"))
    clin <- clin * (1 + eff)
    qd <- exp(theta_of(u, "lq_diff"))
    clcsf <- exp(theta_of(u, "lcl_csf"))
    if (is.na(clcsf)) clcsf <- 0
    if (a != "none" && r$drug == "methotrexate") {
      clcsf <- clcsf * (1 + theta_of(u, "e_conmed_probenecid_cl_csf"))
    }
    ss_rows[[length(ss_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      drug = r$drug,
      arm = if (a == "none") "no inhibitor" else a,
      kpuu_sim = s$Cbrain_ecf / s$Cc,
      kpuu_closed = clin / qd,
      sas_over_ecf_sim = s$Cbrain_csf_sas / s$Cbrain_ecf,
      sas_over_ecf_closed = qd / (qd + clcsf)
    )
  }
}
ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(ss_rows)
knitr::kable(ss, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Unbound brain-ECF/plasma ratio (Kp,uu) and subarachnoid-CSF/ECF ratio at steady state.")
# Both sides use the same parameter values, so the difference is pure ODE
# solver error after a 100-hour infusion.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ss$kpuu_sim / ss$kpuu_closed - 1) < 1e-3),
  all(abs(ss$sas_over_ecf_sim / ss$sas_over_ecf_closed - 1) < 1e-3)
)
```

The P-gp inhibitors raise Kp,uu by 162 % (morphine), 43.4 % (paliperidone),
35.5 % (phenytoin), 443 % (quinidine) and 124 % (risperidone), and
probenecid raises methotrexate's by 409 %, the percentages quoted in the
paper's Results.

# Rat: PKNCA validation

The same mass balance holds over a single dose: everything that enters
brain ECF leaves it through `q_diff`, so AUC(brain ECF) / AUC(plasma) =
`clin / q_diff`. PKNCA computes both AUCs from the typical profiles (no
inhibitor); the published paper reports no NCA values, so this closed form
is the reference.

```{r pknca-rat}
obs_nca <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 60, by = 1), seq(62, 600, by = 4), seq(610, 4320, by = 30))))
nca_runs <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(rat_design))) {
  r <- rat_design[i, ]
  s <- solve_typical(rat_models[[r$drug]],
                     make_events(i, r$dose_mgkg * rat_bw_kg * 1e6, r$dur, obs_nca))
  s$treatment <- r$drug
  s$amt <- r$dose_mgkg * rat_bw_kg * 1e6
  nca_runs[[i]] <- s
}
nca_in <- dplyr::bind_rows(nca_runs) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc, Cbrain_ecf, amt)
dose_df <- nca_in |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, amt) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)

nca_plasma <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals
))
nca_ecf <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cbrain_ecf)), Cbrain_ecf ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals
))
auc_of <- function(res) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
    dplyr::select(treatment, PPORRES)
}
auc_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(
  auc_of(nca_plasma) |> dplyr::rename(auc_plasma = PPORRES),
  auc_of(nca_ecf) |> dplyr::rename(auc_ecf = PPORRES),
  by = "treatment"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ratio_pknca = auc_ecf / auc_plasma,
    ratio_closed = vapply(treatment, function(d) {
      exp(theta_of(rat_ui[[d]], "lclin")) / exp(theta_of(rat_ui[[d]], "lq_diff"))
    }, numeric(1)),
    pct_diff = 100 * (ratio_pknca / ratio_closed - 1)
  )
auc_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Drug" = treatment, "AUCinf plasma (ng*min/mL)" = auc_plasma,
                "AUCinf brain ECF (ng*min/mL)" = auc_ecf,
                "AUC ratio (PKNCA)" = ratio_pknca,
                "clin / q_diff" = ratio_closed, "% difference" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
# Both sides come from the same parameters; the residual is trapezoidal and
# extrapolation error on a dense 72-hour grid.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_cmp$pct_diff) < 3))
```

```{r pknca-rat-table}
as.data.frame(nca_plasma) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename("Drug" = treatment, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (min)" = tmax,
                "Terminal t1/2 (min)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
               caption = "Plasma NCA of the typical rat profiles at the representative doses.")
```

# Human: replicate Figure 6

Figure 6 shows 95 % prediction intervals and medians of 200 simulations for
the translated models. The same is done here: 200 virtual patients per drug
with the Table IV between-subject variability, unbound concentrations.

```{r human-vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170201)
n_sub <- 200
obs_apap <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 60, by = 2), seq(65, 720, by = 10))))
obs_mor <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 30, by = 1), seq(32, 170, by = 4))))
ev_apap <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  make_events(i, 1e9, 30, obs_apap)
}))
ev_mor <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  make_events(i, 1e7, 10, obs_mor)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_apap[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
vpc_apap <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(human_models[["acetaminophen"]]),
                                          ev_apap, useLinCmt = FALSE))
vpc_mor <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(human_models[["morphine"]]),
                                         ev_mor, useLinCmt = FALSE))
vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  vpc_apap |> dplyr::select(time, Plasma = Cc, CSF_SAS = Cbrain_csf_sas, CSF_LV = Cbrain_csf_lv) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "site", values_to = "conc") |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = "Acetaminophen 1 g / 30 min"),
  vpc_mor |> dplyr::select(time, Plasma = Cc, BrainECF = Cbrain_ecf) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "site", values_to = "conc") |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = "Morphine 10 mg / 10 min")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(drug, site, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(lo = quantile(conc, 0.025), med = median(conc),
                   hi = quantile(conc, 0.975), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(vpc, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "red", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(drug ~ site, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Unbound concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates the prediction medians and 95% intervals of Figure 6 of Yamamoto 2017b.")
```

The typical-value comparison against Figure 6 below uses values read off the
figure by the maintainers (approximate; log-scale panels).

```{r human-typical}
typ_apap <- solve_typical(human_models[["acetaminophen"]],
                          make_events(1L, 1e9, 30, obs_apap))
typ_mor <- solve_typical(human_models[["morphine"]],
                         make_events(1L, 1e7, 10, obs_mor))
fig6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel,                                    ~time, ~figure_median, ~model,
  "Acetaminophen plasma",                    300,   1700,  at(typ_apap, 305, "Cc"),
  "Acetaminophen plasma",                    480,   320,   at(typ_apap, 485, "Cc"),
  "Acetaminophen CSF subarachnoid (peak)",   NA,    3500,  max(typ_apap$Cbrain_csf_sas),
  "Acetaminophen CSF subarachnoid",          720,   100,   at(typ_apap, 715, "Cbrain_csf_sas"),
  "Acetaminophen CSF EVD (peak)",            NA,    20000, max(typ_apap$Cbrain_csf_lv),
  "Morphine plasma (peak)",                  NA,    125,   max(typ_mor$Cc),
  "Morphine plasma",                         170,   2.3,   at(typ_mor, 168, "Cc"),
  "Morphine brain ECF, normal side",         50,    8.4,   at(typ_mor, 52, "Cbrain_ecf"),
  "Morphine brain ECF, normal side",         170,   3.5,   at(typ_mor, 168, "Cbrain_ecf")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = model / figure_median)
knitr::kable(fig6, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Typical-value prediction vs the Figure 6 median (figure values approximate).")
# Plasma in both drugs and acetaminophen subarachnoid CSF reproduce the
# published medians within the reading accuracy of a log-scale figure. The
# EVD and morphine brain-ECF rows are known deviations (see Assumptions and
# deviations) and are deliberately not gated.
gate <- fig6[!grepl("EVD|brain ECF", fig6$panel), ]
stopifnot(all(gate$ratio > 0.5 & gate$ratio < 2))
```

## External ventricular drainage

For the EVD patients of Study 1 the lateral-ventricle CSF is drained into
the EVD at a measured, time-varying flow (Table SIV). The model removes it
from `brain_csf_lv` at `CSF_DRAIN_VOL_24H / 24 / 60` mL/min and accumulates
the drained drug in the `evd` state, so the concentration of a collected
sample is the increase of `evd` over the collection interval divided by the
volume collected. Patient 1 of Table SIV (typical parameters, single 1 g
dose, no pre-study acetaminophen):

```{r evd}
# Table SIV patient 1: Q_LV_EVD (mL/h) per collection interval
evd_iv <- tibble::tribble(
  ~start_h, ~end_h, ~q_ml_h,
  0,   0.5, 8,
  0.5, 1,   8,
  1,   1.5, 10,
  1.5, 2,   17,
  2,   2.5, 3,
  2.5, 3,   8,
  3,   3.5, 7,
  3.5, 4,   7,
  4,   5,   2,
  5,   6,   13,
  6,   7,   3,
  7,   8,   7
)
edges <- sort(unique(c(evd_iv$start_h, evd_iv$end_h))) * 60
obs_evd <- sort(unique(c(edges, seq(0, 480, by = 5))))
ev_evd <- make_events(1L, 1e9, 30, obs_evd)
# Time-varying covariate: the flow of the interval that a row opens.
idx <- findInterval(ev_evd$time / 60, evd_iv$start_h, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
ev_evd$CSF_DRAIN_VOL_24H <- evd_iv$q_ml_h[pmax(idx, 1)] * 24
s_evd <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(human_models[["acetaminophen"]])),
  ev_evd, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
))
evd_amt <- s_evd$evd[match(edges, s_evd$time)]
evd_samples <- evd_iv |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    vol_ml = q_ml_h * (end_h - start_h),
    drained_ng = diff(evd_amt),
    C_evd = drained_ng / vol_ml,
    C_lv_mid = s_evd$Cbrain_csf_lv[match(round((start_h + end_h) / 2 * 60 / 5) * 5, s_evd$time)]
  )
knitr::kable(evd_samples, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Simulated EVD sample concentrations (ng/mL) for the Table SIV patient-1 drainage record.")
# The collected sample is lateral-ventricle CSF averaged over the interval,
# so it must lie within the range of C_LV over the whole simulation.
stopifnot(all(evd_samples$C_evd > 0),
          all(evd_samples$C_evd <= max(s_evd$Cbrain_csf_lv) * 1.0001))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Model structure from Figure 2.** The paper describes the structure in a
  diagram rather than in equations. The flow directions follow the arrows of
  Figure 2 and the wording of the Table III footnotes: Q_PL_ECF and Q_LV_PL
  are one-way ("from ... to"), Q_PER and Q_ECF_ICF are bidirectional
  ("inter-compartmental clearance between"), and Q_DIFF carries drug one way
  from brain ECF through the four CSF compartments to plasma. Drug leaving
  plasma into the brain, and returning from the subarachnoid space, is
  booked against the plasma compartment so that mass is conserved; with
  brain volumes of a few hundred microlitres this has no visible effect on
  plasma.
* **Brain ICF and blood-CSF-barrier transport only where estimated.** Table
  III lists the rat V_ICF for every drug, but Q_ECF_ICF was estimable only
  for paliperidone and quinidine and Q_LV_PL only for methotrexate; the other
  models omit those compartments and flows, as the paper's fits did. The
  human models likewise carry no ICF compartment (Table IV has no Q_ECF_ICF).
* **Acetaminophen enterohepatic recirculation.** The paper gives the
  recirculated fraction (93.3 %) but not the equations. The packaged model
  uses the structure of the same group's control stream for the same rat
  acetaminophen data (Yamamoto *et al.* 2017, *CPT Pharmacometrics Syst
  Pharmacol*, Supplementary Material S3): eliminated drug collects in a
  gallbladder compartment that empties at the elimination rate constant, and
  from 120 min after the dose the recirculated fraction of the emptied drug
  returns to plasma. The resulting plateau reproduces Figure 4a.
* **Residual error.** The rat Table III and human Table IV give one residual
  standard deviation per site; the proportional model of Eq. 7 is used,
  which is the only error model in the paper with a single parameter.
* **Acetaminophen rat dose.** Table I gives the acetaminophen dose as
  16 mg/kg; the later paper on the same data gives 15 mg/kg. The vignette
  uses 16 mg/kg; the model itself does not depend on the dose.
* **Human EVD drainage.** The paper adds the EVD flow Q_LV_EVD and the EVD
  volume V_EVD per patient from Table SIV but does not write the equations.
  The model drains lateral-ventricle CSF at the recorded flow into a
  cumulative `evd` state; V_EVD is then the volume collected in an interval
  (Table SIV volumes equal flow times interval length), not a model
  parameter. The patients' pre-study acetaminophen, which the paper entered
  as an initial plasma amount, is not part of the packaged model.
* **Known deviation, acetaminophen CSF EVD.** The median EVD prediction in
  Figure 6a reaches about 2 x 10^4 ng/mL, above the concurrent plasma
  median. In this structure the lateral-ventricle concentration cannot
  exceed what plasma drives through Q_PL_ECF / Q_DIFF = 0.50, so the
  packaged model predicts EVD concentrations about five-fold lower (see the
  table above). The plasma and subarachnoid-CSF panels of the same figure are
  reproduced, so the difference is specific to how the paper's EVD
  compartment was implemented, which is not described.
* **Known deviation, morphine brain ECF.** The Figure 6b median for the
  physiologically normal brain side rises to about 8 ng/mL within 15 min,
  while the packaged model, using the Table IV values exactly, rises over
  about 60 min to about 4 ng/mL; the two converge by 170 min (about 3.2
  versus 3.5 ng/mL). Plasma is reproduced. The values were not adjusted.
* **Morphine dose effect.** Table III reports separate Q_PL_ECF estimates for
  the 4 mg/kg group and the 10/40 mg/kg groups. The model carries the
  10/40 mg/kg value as `lclin` and the 4 mg/kg value through the
  `DOSE_LOW` indicator as the log-ratio `e_dose_low_clin`, so both printed
  values are returned exactly.
* **Phenytoin inhibitor arms.** Phenytoin was studied with tariquidar and
  with tariquidar + probenecid; only a P-gp effect was identified, so
  `CONMED_TARIQUIDAR = 1` for both arms and probenecid has no separate
  effect.
* **External rat validation.** The paper re-estimated the plasma parameters
  of the external acetaminophen and remoxipride rat datasets (Figure 5) but
  does not report them, so Figure 5 is not reproduced here.
* No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (Europe PMC,
  checked 2026-11-25).
